what: A Mixture of Enthusiasts trains: tt-tnt's Llama with 6 of 8 feed-forwards replaced by ttml's sparse MoE
result: Forward, backward, optimiser step, loss descending, on one Blackhole card.

smoke.throughput: ~7 it/s at batch 8 on a single chip once warm

architecture.why_10_experts: one per corpus source, which is what the die regions were measured over
architecture.why_2_dense_blocks: the earliest blocks do position and syntax, which every token needs; the shipped DeepSeek config uses n_dense_layers: 2 for the same reason
architecture.why_width_928: top-2 plus one shared gives 0.989x the dense model's ACTIVE parameters. That is the only sizing under which an MoE arm and the dense control are comparable; the obvious smaller width gives 0.38x and would lose on capacity while appearing to say something about routing.

how_it_is_possible_in_twenty_lines.the_seam: ttml/models/llama/transformer.py:177 holds the feed-forward as a plain attribute, self.mlp = LlamaMLP(...), and LlamaMLP.forward and SparseMoEEP.forward have the identical signature forward(Tensor) -> Tensor.
how_it_is_possible_in_twenty_lines.separability: SparseMoEEP imports ttnn, ttml, .moe and .autograd_ops, and nothing from DeepSeek's attention. The MoE feed-forward is separable from the model family that ships it.
how_it_is_possible_in_twenty_lines.why_not_subclass_Llama: Llama.__init__ builds its own ModuleList of blocks. Injecting a block type means duplicating that construction and keeping the duplicate in step with upstream forever; reassigning block.mlp touches one attribute and inherits future changes.

what_this_corrects: An earlier note in this session stated that MoE would force tt-tnt onto the DeepSeek model family -- MLA attention, a nope/rope head split, and a NEW EMBEDDING MATRIX that would have invalidated artifacts/token_core_map.npz and every die-region measurement with it. True of the shipped configs, false of the module. tt-tnt keeps GQA, RoPE, its tokenizer, its vocabulary and its die map.
what_this_is_NOT: Not a quality result. Twenty steps at batch 8 shows the machinery runs; it says nothing about whether the MoE is better than the dense model.

Not the four-arm experiment. The gate here is stock (learned) -- the control arm. The seeded and frozen policies, which are the ones that connect the die to the router, are declared and NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

Not load-balanced. This run used plain Voronoi routing at 7.66x imbalance, which matters for a frozen gate and not for a learned one. --moe-balance exists and gives 1.50x, and is a DIFFERENT routing from the one whose register effect was measured.
next: Implement seeded/frozen gate initialisation, then run the arms: dense (already trained, val 2.9570), learned, seeded, frozen. The measurement most worth having is whether a free gate drifts toward or away from the measured die regions.
